_description: Known-answer test vector for the Layer-2 payload encryption protocol (ECDH-P256 + HKDF-SHA256 + AES-256-GCM), generated from the server's own primitives (apps.core.payload_crypto). Use this to unit-test a new client implementation (Flutter/Dart, etc.) without needing a running server: if your port computes the same derived_aes_key_hex and can decrypt gcm2_token back to plaintext, it is byte-compatible with the server.
_warning: These private keys are test-only and intentionally public. Never reuse this key material for anything real.
point_encoding: X9.62 uncompressed point, urlsafe-base64 (no padding stripped)
how_to_use: 1. Derive a private key from client_private_key_int_hex on your target curve (P-256) -- or simply hardcode client_public_key_b64u / server_public_key_b64u and skip private-key derivation if your library only exposes point math, not scalar-to-keypair import.
2. Run ECDH between the client private key and server_public_key_b64u (or server private key + client_public_key_b64u) -- either direction must yield shared_secret_hex.
3. Run HKDF-SHA256(shared_secret, salt=empty, info='hospital-crm-payload-v1', length=32) -- must yield derived_aes_key_hex.
4. AES-256-GCM-decrypt gcm2_token's nonce+ciphertext with derived_aes_key_hex, no AAD -- must yield plaintext_utf8 exactly.

5. Optionally also AES-256-GCM-ENCRYPT plaintext_utf8 with derived_aes_key_hex and nonce_hex -- must yield the same ciphertext bytes embedded in gcm2_token (confirms your encrypt path, not just decrypt).
generated_by: Backend/apps/core/payload_crypto.py primitives, verified via a round-trip through the real decrypt_payload() function -- see docs/API_ENCRYPTION_GUIDE.md §9
